claims.statement: WHO's laboratory quality-management handbook is based on ISO 15189 and covers essential quality-management topics across clinical and public-health laboratory processes.
WHO quality-system guidance explicitly includes internal and third-party quality control, external quality assessment, continuous improvement, and regular review and analysis of testing data.

contrary_evidence: Modern analyzers and laboratory information systems already include QC charts and rule alerts.
A reagent vendor may resist exposing cross-site lot problems that could increase claims.

economics.acquisition_route: Begin with CSV exports from 3-5 consenting labs recruited by one regional IVD distributor, then prove earlier root-cause isolation.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 2500 analyzers at 300 PLN monthly net revenue yield 9m PLN ARR; at 32% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 60% founder ownership, equity is about 6.9m PLN in year 6-9. Retained cash is not added again.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-18 hours weekly, with a laboratory quality specialist contracted for validation and alert policy.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 75-85% after ingestion, alert review, and support once a connector is reused across sites.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 15000-35000 PLN onboarding cost per distributor recovered within 6-10 months at 20 connected analyzers.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 250-600 PLN per connected analyzer monthly, with a distributor portfolio minimum and paid connector setup.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Analyzer and reagent contracts are multi-year; every new QC run and reagent lot is a repeat event.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Cross-laboratory, confirmed reagent-lot and instrument-behavior benchmarks improve detection beyond any single site
fingerprint.customer: Clinical laboratories using analyzers and reagent lots supplied by an IVD distributor
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: IVD distributors bundle the service into reagent, analyzer, and support contracts with recurring lab buyers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Cross-site QC drift detection, lot benchmarking, and investigation packets sold as portfolio-quality SaaS
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Distributor or vendor pays a recurring fee per connected analyzer or laboratory site
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Quality-control values shift, a lot performs inconsistently, or support must distinguish instrument, reagent, and process causes

founder_fit: Statistical process control and anomaly detection closely match the founder's training.
The model sells through a small number of reagent distributors rather than many laboratories.
A software-only pilot can stay within capital and part-time limits if it begins with file exports.
risks: Missed or false drift alerts can affect laboratory decisions.
The product may fall under IVDR depending on intended purpose and claims.
Instrument vendors may block data access or bundle a competing feature.

structure.control_point: Network benchmark for reagent-lot and analyzer QC behavior
structure.critical_dependency: Permissioned QC data from enough labs using a common reagent or analyzer family

thesis: Let IVD reagent distributors bundle a QC analytics layer with the instruments and reagents they repeatedly sell to small and mid-sized laboratories. The service ingests de-identified control measurements, detects within-lab drift, compares a reagent lot across participating sites, and creates an investigation packet for the lab and distributor. The distributor reduces support ambiguity and protects reagent relationships; pooled confirmed issues become a difficult-to-recreate lot-performance asset.
title: Reagent-Lot Drift Sentinel
uncertainties: Can enough labs share de-identified QC data under their quality agreements?
Which analyzer export or middleware interface offers the cheapest initial integration?
Will distributors pay for fewer support cases or will labs need to be the payer?
